1.why: Every /api route after login goes through requireSession, and MFA records are read via records.get(session.userId) with getSession additionally verifying session.userId === USER.id, so MFA settings are bound to the server-side session owner with no client-supplied identifiers.

2.why: Identity codes are stored per-session as a single-use digest in session.identity and TOTP secrets live in the per-user record, so a code issued to one session cannot verify another session or user.

3.why: /api/totp/verify sets record.enabled = true but never removes other entries from the sessions map, so previously issued sessions remain valid until logout or timeout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is AES-GCM encrypted via encrypt() and backup codes are stored only as PBKDF2-SHA256 verifiers with per-code salts, never in plaintext.

5.why: token() and randomFrom() use crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling for codes, secrets, and salts; only the opt-in MFA_TEST_MODE substitutes fixed fixtures.

6.why: The only cookie is mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict, and the client holds the CSRF token and recovery codes solely in JS variables, never in localStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: The server validates all input: email regex plus length bounds, password length limits, ^\d{6}$ for OTPs, a strict recovery-code pattern, and JSON content-type/shape checks in body().

8.why: All client-side rendering of dynamic values passes through esc() or textContent, and the nonce-based CSP (script-src 'nonce-…', base-uri 'none') prevents execution of injected markup or script.

9.why: safePath() limits the post-login 'next' value to a fixed allow-list of internal paths, and the client router whitelists hash routes, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() and clearSessionCookie() both emit HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict attributes on the session cookie.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the client log() function and on-page Logs panel print the identity code, authenticator secret, provisioning URI and recovery codes to the browser console, so secrets do end up in logs.

13.why: Identity codes carry an expires timestamp (20 min) and used flag enforced in matches(), TOTP replay is blocked via usedCounters, and backup codes are marked used on consumption.

14.why: failed() counts failures and locked() imposes a 5-minute lockout after 5 failures on the identity, TOTP and recovery verification endpoints.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a fresh token(32) identifier, getSession enforces 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
